description: An approximate-equality expectation checks whether two integer operands are within a tolerance (epsilon) of one another. The outcome is a pass when the absolute difference between the two operands is strictly less than epsilon, and a fail otherwise. The engine renders the expression as the left operand, a tilde, then the right operand and the epsilon shown as a plus-or-minus tolerance inside parentheses. These cases probe the strict-inequality boundary where the difference equals epsilon, a zero tolerance, a non-positive tolerance, and negative operands.
